description: The semantic overlay that relates the function modules without editing them. It holds business functions and seats, decision rights and answerability, boundary objects and each function's perspective on them, handoffs and what they transfer, outcomes and metric definitions (never values), and attributable, provenance-bearing claims. The central claim is the cross-boundary effect claim, which the module holds but never asserts as true.
documentation:
# Cross-Functional Core module (xfn)

Each existing module (hr, lgl, cmp, fin, log) is one function's local vocabulary. `xfn` is the only module whose classes describe relations **between** other modules' instances. Its edges always start at `xfn` nodes, point into the function modules, and never the other way round, so `xfn` can be reseeded or removed without breaking any local site.

**Five things `xfn` keeps apart**
- **Structure (fact).** `xfn:BusinessFunction` is what is done, not `hr:OrgUnit`, which is who is grouped. `xfn:Position` is a seat that survives turnover. `xfn:Handoff` + `xfn:Transfer` record what crosses a boundary and whether the receiver accepted it.
- **Accountability (fact).** `xfn:DecisionRight`, `xfn:Answerability` and `xfn:MetricBinding` are sourced, time-bounded records held by seats. `xfn:ExposureGap` is derived only; it shows where one seat decides what another seat bears.
- **Meaning (convention).** `xfn:BoundaryObject` is a thin anchor. Each function's view of it is an `xfn:Perspective` pointing at that function's own records (never `owl:sameAs`). Disagreements are `xfn:PerspectiveCorrespondence` records: graded, attributed, never resolved in favour of one function.
- **Definition without value.** `xfn:Variable` names a neutral state. `xfn:Outcome` says which direction of it is desired and whose remit it is. `xfn:MetricDefinition` / `xfn:MetricVersion` say what a number would mean. Values live in the measurement layer, keyed by `xfn:MetricVersion` IRI.
- **Claims (held, never asserted).** `xfn:EffectClaim` is the arrow: an n-ary node relating a cause `xfn:Variable` to an effect `xfn:Variable`, usually via an `xfn:Decision`. It records sign, rung, lag, claimant, function and evidence. **No property links two Variables directly.** Verdicts, including the causal engine's, arrive only as `xfn:Appraisal` records.

**Rules of the house**
- Every claim has exactly one `xfn:attributedTo` and one `xfn:onBehalfOf`.
- `xfn:recordStatus` is a speech-act lifecycle (`draft|asserted|withdrawn|superseded`); none of its values means true.
- Records freeze when they leave draft. A change is a new record that `xfn:revises` the old one.
- Instance IRIs follow `xfn:<Class>/<stable-id>`, are never reused, and are retired rather than deleted.
- Multi-valued facts are object properties, never propsJson arrays.

Nothing here computes a value, a causal verdict, a weight, a score or a rollup.

classes.label: AttributedRecord
classes.definition: Abstract root. An immutable information entity attributed to exactly one answerable agent. It records that someone said, defined, recorded or stipulated something, and when. It never records that the thing is true. Content freezes when the record leaves draft; a change is a new record that revises it. Aligned to prov:Entity.

classes.label: ControlledTerm
classes.definition: A term in one of the module's open, governed vocabularies, held as instance data (like log:Incoterm). Terms are grouped by xfn:termScheme: evidence-class, appraisal-aspect, divergence-mode, carried-kind, decision-kind, commitment-kind, decision-context. Adding a term is a data change, not a schema change. Aligned to skos:Concept.

classes.label: AnalyticAgent
classes.definition: A versioned software agent that authors claims, appraisals or evidence: a causal engine, an insight rule, a forecasting model. It always has an accountable human or organisational owner. A new version is a new agent. Aligned to prov:SoftwareAgent.

classes.label: Deliberation
classes.definition: An occasion on which records were produced about one or more decisions: a CEO decision review, an S&OP meeting, a structured elicitation, an analysis run, a post-incident review, an audit. It gathers every C-suite input on one decision. It also shows whether each claim was solicited (claimant is not the convener) or volunteered. Aligned to prov:Activity.

classes.label: BusinessFunction
classes.definition: A durable domain of business responsibility: Procurement, Finance, Operations, Customer Support, Legal & Compliance, Revenue, People, Product & Engineering, and 'Enterprise' for the CEO's whole-business remit. It has a stable key that survives reorganisation. It is deliberately not hr:OrgUnit: functions map many-to-many onto the reporting tree, and Acme has no Procurement, Support or Legal OrgUnit at all. Aligned to ArchiMate Business Function.

classes.label: Position
classes.definition: A seat in the organisation that exists independently of whoever fills it, e.g. 'Chief Procurement Officer' or 'S&OP Council'. It instantiates an hr:Role and sits in an hr:OrgUnit. Decision rights, answerabilities and metric bindings attach to seats, not people, so accountability survives turnover. A collective seat (committee, board) is a Position with positionKind 'collective'. Aligned to org:Post.

classes.label: BoundaryObject
classes.definition: An entity or concept that two or more functions each touch and represent differently for their own work (Star & Griesemer): a supplier, a supply arrangement, a product, the concept 'on-time', the concept 'savings'. It is deliberately thin: a scope statement every function accepts, its form, and an optional steward. All descriptive content lives in Perspectives, so no function's view is privileged. Ideal-type boundary objects are the reference hub for terminology; instance boundary objects are the join key across modules' records.

classes.label: LegalEntity
classes.definition: A registered legal person (company, branch, natural person) identified by LEI or registration number, never by any function's master-data key. It is the real-world referent that a fin:Vendor payee row, an lgl:Party signatory, a log:Carrier and an hr:Contractor agency may each be about. It is not called Party because lgl:Party already names a role. It carries the corporate parent, which insight rule R1 needs to be evaluated at group grain. Aligned to OMG Commons cmns-pts:Party and GLEIF LegalEntity.

classes.label: Perspective
classes.definition: One business function's partial, purpose-bound view of one boundary object. It records the module-native records that represent the object for that function (representedBy), the work the view serves, the operational criterion applied, the module class seen through, and how the identity match was made. It is a reified relator: function x object x records x criterion x valid time. It is the sanctioned replacement for owl:sameAs and for cross-module pointer edges. Two perspectives may disagree, and neither is wrong because of that.

classes.label: PerspectiveCorrespondence
classes.definition: An attributed, graded statement of how one function's perspective relates to others on the same boundary object: exact, close, broad, narrow or related match, or an explicit denial. It names the facet, the kind of knowledge boundary (syntactic, semantic or pragmatic), the decision contexts it is claimed for, and the steward's adoption decision. It is the only place terminology collisions are recorded, and it never names a winner: 'reconciled' means a shared translation was agreed, and 'plural' means both views stand.

classes.label: Handoff
classes.definition: A standing, directed interface across which one function passes work, material, information, obligations, authority, resources, cost or risk to another, for a kind of boundary object (e.g. 'Procurement to Operations: supplier onboarding'). It carries the receiver's own requirement: the next process is the customer. It is type-level; individual POs and tickets are event data keyed to the Handoff IRI in the measurement layer.

classes.label: Transfer
classes.definition: One element carried across a functional boundary, attached either to a standing Handoff or to a specific Decision or Commitment. It records what is carried, the milestone at which it passes, whether the receiver has accepted it, its basis (designed, contractual or observed practice, never 'claimed'), and the instrument that fixes it. An unacknowledged cost or risk transfer is an internal externality by construction. It subsumes 'obligation borne by', 'cost borne by' and acceptance of an obligation assignment.

classes.label: AccountabilityAssertion
classes.definition: Abstract. A sourced, time-bounded fact about what one seat holds, owes or is evaluated on. Its basis is either formal (conferred by an instrument) or attested (observed practice, with evidence). It records the forum answered to. It is immutable once in force; a change supersedes it.

classes.label: DecisionRight
classes.definition: The holder seat may exercise a right of a stated kind (initiate, ratify, veto, implement, monitor, consult, inform) over one DecisionDomain, within an optional monetary limit and scope, traceable by delegation to a root right. With basis 'attested' it records real authority, i.e. who actually decides (Aghion & Tirole).

classes.label: Answerability
classes.definition: The holder seat must render account to a forum for an object: an Outcome, cmp:Risk, cmp:Control, fin:CostCenter, lgl:Contract or BoundaryObject, or, as definition-steward, for a term. This is Bovens' actor-forum-object relation with the sanctions leg excluded, because sanctions are incentive design. It is the factual record of consequence exposure.

classes.label: MetricBinding
classes.definition: The holder seat is formally evaluated on (evaluated-on), or must report (reports-on), a MetricDefinition for a fiscal period. This is what a role is scored on, recorded as fact only: no weight, target, threshold or payout. Its IRI is the join key the measurement and incentive layers attach their own data to.

classes.label: DecisionDomain
classes.definition: A class of decisions, i.e. a lever, such as 'supplier selection, direct materials' or 'standard payment terms'. It is owned by exactly one BusinessFunction and acts on one kind of entity. Its IRI is the stable, type-level handle an external causal model binds an intervention variable family to. The ontology never states what a domain affects.

classes.label: ExposureGap
classes.definition: DERIVED ONLY; never hand-asserted. It is produced when all of the following hold: seat P has an in-force ratify or veto DecisionRight over domain D; an asserted EffectClaim concerns a decision in D; a different seat Q has an Answerability for the outcome of the claimed effect; and P has no answerability of its own for that outcome. The result: P decides what Q bears. The gap records where the two ends first converge in the solid-line hierarchy and on shared forums. It is conditional on the claim and asserts nothing about the claim's truth. Its IRI is deterministic over (right, answerability, claim).

classes.label: Decision
classes.definition: A dated, attributable act, or proposed act, of authority by a named person in a named function: a supplier switch, payment-terms change, budget cut, hiring freeze, capitalisation ruling, concession, roadmap deferral, expedite. It records who decided, when, in which capacity and under which right, which functions were consulted, what the decision sets (the do() target: variables, baseline and new state), and the rationale stated at the time. It says nothing about consequences. It is the intervention anchor for the causal layer and the usual subject of effect claims. It replaces every per-function decision class; the kind is a ControlledTerm.

classes.label: Commitment
classes.definition: A promise to or from an external counterparty that binds another function's options or performance: a volume or exclusivity commitment, a spend commitment with exit cost, a customer service entitlement, a forward roadmap or delivery promise, a concession. It records whether it is contractual, where it is actually captured (contract, order form, email, verbal, none), and which decision made it. Who bears it internally is recorded as a Transfer. The defining property of the class is how often isContractual is false.

classes.label: TermDeviation
classes.definition: A reified gap between what a contract says about a risk-allocating term (indemnity, liability cap, warranty, termination right, payment terms, SLA) and a stated standard or benchmark contract. Direction 'absent' covers an expected term that is missing, since an absence cannot otherwise be a node. It records who approved the deviation and when, which is usually empty. It asserts no consequence; consequences are EffectClaims that may cite it.

classes.label: Variable
classes.definition: A named, neutral state or quantity of the business that claims are about, e.g. 'primary supplier of component C', 'weekly defect tickets on product P', 'indemnity cover on component C'. It is the construct: not its metric, not its values, not a valence. It must be observable in principle, so 'savings', 'uplift' and 'impact' are EffectClaims with a contrast, not Variables. It is attributed to whoever defined it, so rival definitions are distinct Variables. Variables are never linked to other Variables.

classes.label: Outcome
classes.definition: A state of the business someone values: a Variable plus the desired direction of it, phrased as a desirable condition and placed in one or more functions' remit. A shared outcome is, by definition, made up of outcomes in two or more remits (hasConstituent). That make-up is definitional, never causal, and forms the DAG that propagation walks. An Outcome holds no values, targets, baselines or weights.

classes.label: MetricDefinition
classes.definition: The enduring catalogue identity of a named metric (e.g. 'Procurement unit-cost saving', 'OTIF') and its governance facts: which function defines and reports it, which seat stewards it, which forum receives it. Names are deliberately not unique across definitions. Two definitions both called 'OTIF' are two metrics, and that collision is the point. A MetricDefinition has no operational meaning of its own; meaning lives in its versions.

classes.label: MetricVersion
classes.definition: One immutable operational definition of a metric: plain-language meaning; population (class plus inclusion and exclusion rules, optionally pinned to one function's Perspective); a computation description, not an implementation; baseline; recognition event; clock and measurement boundary; unit; scale type; stock/flow type; and grain. It is the only node a measurement system may bind a value to. Any change of meaning mints a new version that supersedes it with a declared comparability.

classes.label: DimensionBinding
classes.definition: Declares that a metric version's observations are indexed by one GrainDimension, at a fixed position in the observation key, with a fixed rollup rule along that dimension. A version's set of bindings is its grain. It is what tells the propagation layer what is joinable and how aggregation is permitted.

classes.label: GrainDimension
classes.definition: A conformed dimension along which observations are indexed and joined: org unit, cost center, vendor, legal entity, SKU, fiscal period, calendar week. It names the KG class whose instances are its coordinates and the KG predicate that forms its hierarchy (e.g. hr:parentUnit). Metrics that share no non-temporal dimension can meet only at the enterprise total. That is the Ashby attenuating channel, made visible.

classes.label: Claim
classes.definition: Abstract. An attributed assertion that can itself be appraised. It keeps the author's own words verbatim beside its structured encoding, along with the evidence the author cites and the author's own stated confidence. Holding a claim never asserts its content. Aligned to schema:Claim.

classes.label: EffectClaim
ProxyClaim
classes.definition: An attributed claim that a metric indicates the state of an outcome. It records the question the metric actually answers, the direction claimed to signal progress, the ceteris-paribus conditions under which that holds, and which constituents of the outcome it covers. The gap between the operational question and the outcome statement is where Goodhart lives. Constituents that no proxy covers are the tasks Holmstrom-Milgrom predict will be neglected.

classes.label: DivergenceClaim
classes.definition: An attributed claim that under a stated trigger a proxy breaks: the metric improves while its outcome, or another function's outcome, does not or gets worse. It records the divergence modes (regressional, extremal, causal, adversarial, multitask-omission, externality, horizon-mismatch), the outcomes at risk, the counter-metrics that would reveal the break, and references to the EffectClaims describing the mechanism. It subsumes knownSubstitutionRisk, knownGamingVector, proxyGap and excludedSignal.

classes.label: ForecastClaim
classes.definition: A dated, owner-attributed claim about the future value of a metric version for a period and scope. It records the method, the revision chain (via revises), and the functions that declare they plan against it. The numeric value is held by the measurement layer, keyed by this IRI. The revision topology alone makes sandbagging and late convergence visible, and consumedBy gives each revision a known blast radius.

classes.label: Appraisal
classes.definition: An attributed position that one agent takes on an existing record: endorses, disputes, qualifies, not-identifiable or abstains. It names the aspects concerned and may advance rival records, such as a counter-claim or a rival variable definition. This is the only way a verdict, from a person or from the causal engine, enters the ontology. The appraised record is never changed, and appraisals are never aggregated here. It subsumes contests, counterClaim, disputedBy and Contestation.

classes.label: EvidenceItem
Reading
classes.definition: One community's interpretation of an artefact whose meaning depends on vocabulary (an insight rule, NLQ intent, report or scorecard line): the Perspectives it takes each term from, and the identity criterion it joins records on. Several readings of one artefact can coexist, e.g. Finance's, Legal's and Procurement's readings of R1. It makes the artefact's hidden vocabulary choices queryable without deciding which reading is right.

properties.name: attributedTo
properties.definition: The single agent who answers for the record: claimant, author, preparer or recorder (prov:wasAttributedTo). Joint positions are separate records or endorsing appraisals, never co-authorship. Cross-module axiom: range stored null in PROP_DEFS and enforced by SHACL.

properties.name: onBehalfOf
properties.definition: The function whose position the record speaks for. Required on every Claim and on any record attributed to an AnalyticAgent. Makes the claimant's incentive position legible as structure without scoring it.

properties.name: recordedAt
properties.definition: When the author made the statement or definition (prov:generatedAtTime). Set once and never back-dated, which is what separates an ex-ante forecast from an ex-post explanation.

properties.name: recordStatus
properties.definition: Speech-act lifecycle only: draft | asserted | withdrawn | superseded. Only draft records are mutable. No value means verified, accepted, true or false, and none will be added.

properties.name: withdrawnAt
properties.definition: When the author withdrew the record. Withdrawn records stay in the graph; withdrawal is never deletion.

properties.name: revises
properties.definition: The earlier record of the same class that this one replaces (prov:wasRevisionOf). The earlier record keeps its IRI and content and is marked superseded.

properties.name: contentDigest
properties.definition: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the record's content properties (Ontos audit canonicalize(), object values as IRIs). Excludes recordStatus, withdrawnAt, decisionStatus and itself. Required once asserted. A changed digest under the same IRI is a detectable contract violation.

properties.name: generatedIn
properties.definition: The occasion that produced the record (prov:wasGeneratedBy).

properties.name: validFrom
properties.definition: Start of business validity (valid time) of a Position, Perspective, AccountabilityAssertion, Handoff or Outcome. Shared property with no rdfs:domain (null slot), so nothing is inferred from having it.

properties.name: validTo
properties.definition: End of business validity, inclusive. Absent means still valid. Shared property with no rdfs:domain.

properties.name: termScheme
properties.definition: The vocabulary the term belongs to: evidence-class | appraisal-aspect | divergence-mode | carried-kind | decision-kind | commitment-kind | decision-context. It is also the first segment of the term's local id (xfn:ControlledTerm/evidence-class.natural-experiment).

properties.name: termDefinition
properties.definition: Normative definition of the term (skos:definition).

properties.name: broaderTerm
properties.definition: A more general term in the same scheme (skos:broader). Lets consumers fall back from an unknown new term to one they know.

properties.name: agentVersion
properties.definition: Software version. A new version is a new agent, so results are never pooled across versions.

properties.name: accountableOwner
properties.definition: The person or unit that answers for the agent's output (prov:actedOnBehalfOf). Software never answers for itself.

properties.name: deliberationKind
properties.definition: decision-review | structured-elicitation | analysis-run | post-incident-review | audit | ad-hoc.

properties.name: startedAt
properties.definition: When the occasion began.

properties.name: convenedBy
properties.definition: Who convened or ran the occasion. A claim made there by anyone else was solicited; otherwise it was volunteered.

properties.name: concernsDecision
properties.definition: The decisions (enacted, or proposed options) under deliberation. This is the hook that gathers every C-suite input on one CEO decision.

properties.name: functionKey
properties.definition: Stable machine key: procurement, finance, operations, support, legal, revenue, people, engineering, enterprise. It never changes and survives reorganisation and renaming.

properties.name: performedBy
properties.definition: Org units that currently carry out the function. Many-to-many, so a reorg does not rewrite function-level facts. A function with none is itself a finding.

properties.name: headedBy
properties.definition: The seat accountable for the function (the C-suite member), as fact.

properties.name: vocabularyPrefix
properties.definition: Prefix of the Ontos module that is this function's native vocabulary (fin, lgl, cmp, log, hr). Absent for functions that have no module yet.

properties.name: subFunctionOf
properties.definition: Functional decomposition, e.g. Treasury under Finance. Acyclic.

properties.name: instantiatesRole
properties.definition: The job-role type the seat instantiates. Gives hr:Role's promised 'responsibility set' a home: the accountability assertions held by seats of that role.

properties.name: positionIn
properties.definition: The org unit the seat sits in. Reuses the hr:OrgUnit tree unchanged.

properties.name: positionKind
properties.definition: individual | collective. Collective seats (Board, ExCo, S&OP Council) may have several concurrent holders.

properties.name: solidLineTo
properties.definition: Supervisory reporting line between seats. Must form one rooted acyclic tree at any instant. hr:reportsTo (person-level, HRIS-sourced) is kept unchanged.

properties.name: dottedLineTo
properties.definition: Functional or matrix reporting lines: the lateral channels the solid hierarchy attenuates.

properties.name: seatOn
properties.definition: Ex officio membership of a collective seat, e.g. CPO seatOn S&OP Council. Makes cross-functional forums explicit convergence points.

properties.name: scopeStatement
properties.definition: The agreed identity and extent of the object; the only content every perspective accepts, e.g. 'supply of component C to all product lines, whichever supplier'. For ideal-type objects it is the reference definition.

properties.name: boundaryForm
properties.definition: Star & Griesemer form: idealType (a concept, e.g. 'supplier', 'on-time', 'savings') | coincidentBoundaries (an instance, e.g. this supply arrangement) | standardizedForm (a medium, e.g. the PO form) | repository.

properties.name: exemplifies
properties.definition: Links an instance object to the ideal-type object it is a case of. Also defines unit populations for the causal layer.

properties.name: aboutEntity
properties.definition: Shared property, no rdfs:domain, open range. On a BoundaryObject: the real-world referent it denotes, normally an xfn:LegalEntity or an authority IRI such as an ELI. On a Variable: the entities whose state it describes (log:InventoryItem, fin:Vendor, hr:OrgUnit, log:Route). It may never point at another Variable. Cross-module.

properties.name: stewardedBy
properties.definition: Shared property, no rdfs:domain. On a BoundaryObject: the boundary spanner accountable across all its perspectives. On a MetricDefinition: the definitional steward. Absence on a BoundaryObject is the anchor-scenario finding that nobody owns both ends.

properties.name: legalName
properties.definition: Registered legal name as incorporated. Not the trading name on the vendor master, and not the brand Procurement negotiated with.

properties.name: lei
properties.definition: ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier. The preferred identity basis. A property, never the IRI.

properties.name: registrationId
properties.definition: Company registration or tax identifier in the jurisdiction of incorporation.

properties.name: incorporatedIn
properties.definition: Jurisdiction of incorporation. Reuses Legal's jurisdiction class.

properties.name: parentEntity
properties.definition: Direct consolidating parent (GLEIF Level 2). Acyclic. Its transitive closure is what makes 'do we have a contract with this group' answerable, and makes R1 correct at group grain.

properties.name: heldBy
properties.definition: The function whose view this is.

properties.name: perspectiveOn
properties.definition: The boundary object viewed.

properties.name: representedBy
properties.definition: The module-native records through which this function represents the object: fin:Vendor/V-2291, lgl:Party/PTY-017, lgl:Contract/..., log:PurchaseOrder/..., hr:Contractor/... Open cross-module range (null slot). This is correspondence without merging, and the only sanctioned identity link across modules.

properties.name: localPurpose
properties.definition: The work the view serves, e.g. 'pay accurately and control spend', 'allocate liability'.

properties.name: localCriterion
properties.definition: The operational definition the function applies to count, classify or accept the object, e.g. 'vendor = unblocked remit-to payee paid in last 18 months' or 'on-time = despatched by latest confirmed promise'. Different criteria on one object are expected, not errors.

properties.name: localClass
properties.definition: CURIE of the module class through which the function sees the object (fin:Vendor, lgl:Party). Needed on ideal-type objects, where perspectives are definitions rather than records.

properties.name: identityBasis
properties.definition: How the representation was matched to the object: lei-match | registry-id-match | tax-id-match | shared-source-key | name-similarity | signature-block | manual. Identity across modules is an attributable assertion, not a given.

properties.name: revisedBy
properties.definition: The decision that produced this perspective version, e.g. the Legal perspective pointing at the new contract after a supplier switch. Enables before/after comparison.

properties.name: correspondenceSubject
properties.definition: The perspective the statement is about.

properties.name: correspondenceObject
properties.definition: The other perspective(s) on the same boundary object. More than one only with compoundOperator.

properties.name: matchRelation
properties.definition: exact | close | broad | narrow | related, with SKOS semantics: 'subject broad object' means the object is broader.

properties.name: negated
properties.definition: True = an explicit, attributed denial that the relation holds (SSSOM predicate_modifier 'Not'). Distinct from no record, which means unknown.

properties.name: compoundOperator
properties.definition: AND | OR over multiple objects (ISO 25964-2), e.g. Sales on-time = AND(line in-full, generation-1 date). Required exactly when there is more than one object.

properties.name: hierarchyType
properties.definition: generic | partitive | instance; required for broad and narrow. A partitive-narrower concept (unit price within total cost of ownership) is a component and never stands for its whole.

properties.name: divergenceFacet
properties.definition: The aspect on which the views relate or differ, in neutral words: 'identity grain', 'clock start', 'baseline', 'cost elements included'.

properties.name: divergenceKind
properties.definition: Carlile boundary type: syntactic (different terms, same meaning) | semantic (different meanings) | pragmatic (different interests at stake).

properties.name: adoptionStatus
properties.definition: proposed | adopted | rejected | reconciled | plural. The steward's decision on the convention; it changes at most once, and later changes are revisions. 'reconciled' = a shared translation agreed; 'plural' = legitimately different, both kept. No value names a winning function. Exists only on conventions, never on empirical claims.

properties.name: appliesInContext
properties.definition: Decision contexts (scheme decision-context: ctx.all, ctx.payables, ctx.spend-analytics, ctx.causal-modelling, ctx.performance-reporting) in which the convention is claimed to hold.

properties.name: reviewedBy
properties.definition: The steward who adopted or rejected the record. Required once adoptionStatus is not 'proposed'.

properties.name: handoffFrom
properties.definition: The providing function.

properties.name: handoffTo
properties.definition: The receiving function. Must differ from the provider.

properties.name: concernsObject
properties.definition: The boundary object (usually an ideal type) whose instances cross this interface.

properties.name: mediatedBy
properties.definition: The standardized-form boundary object that carries the handoff (PO form, ticket, contract template).

properties.name: receiverCriterion
properties.definition: What the receiving function requires of what it receives, in its own terms, e.g. 'supplier qualified at part-revision grain before first PO'. A definition, not a target, and the basis on which 'doing better for other departments' becomes checkable.

properties.name: formality
properties.definition: formal (designed, documented interface) | informal (observed practice with no designed interface).

properties.name: transferOf
properties.definition: The standing handoff, specific decision or commitment carrying this element. Union range stored null; enforced by SHACL-SPARQL.

properties.name: transferTo
properties.definition: The receiving function, e.g. obligation borne by Operations, cost borne by Logistics. Implied by handoffTo on a Handoff; required when transferOf is a Decision or Commitment.

properties.name: carriesKind
properties.definition: Term in scheme carried-kind: work, material, information, obligation, authority, resource (substance handed over), or cost, risk (consequence allocated).

properties.name: passesAt
properties.definition: The milestone at which this element passes, e.g. 'contract execution', 'goods receipt'. Risk and cost may pass at different points, as under the Incoterms C-rules.

properties.name: acceptanceStatus
properties.definition: accepted | acknowledged | disputed | unacknowledged. 'Asserted by the sender' and 'accepted by the receiver' are different events; the gap between them is the finding.

properties.name: acceptedBy
properties.definition: The person in the receiving function who accepted. Required when acceptanceStatus = accepted.

properties.name: transferBasis
properties.definition: designed | contractual | observedPractice. 'claimed' is deliberately not a value: alleged transfers are EffectClaims.

properties.name: governedBy
properties.definition: The instrument that fixes the transfer: lgl:Clause, log:Incoterm, cmp:Policy, or a finance cost-allocation rule node. Open cross-module range (null slot).

properties.name: refersToItem
properties.definition: The registered item carried, held in the module that owns it: cmp:Risk, lgl:Obligation, fin:CostCenter, log:InventoryItem. Open cross-module range (null slot); xfn links into each function's vocabulary instead of duplicating it.

properties.name: holder
properties.definition: The seat that holds, owes or is evaluated on this. Always a Position, never a Person.

properties.name: basis
properties.definition: formal (conferred by an instrument; grantedUnder required) | attested (observed practice; evidenceRef required).

properties.name: grantedUnder
properties.definition: The governing instrument, e.g. the Delegation-of-Authority policy cmp:Policy/POL-03. Required when basis = formal.

properties.name: evidenceRef
properties.definition: Evidence of observed practice. Required when basis = attested.

properties.name: answerableTo
properties.definition: The forum or principal seat. Absent only for the root seat.

properties.name: overDomain
properties.definition: The lever the right applies to.

properties.name: rightKind
properties.definition: initiate | ratify | veto | implement | monitor | consult | inform: the Fama & Jensen decision process plus participation rights.

properties.name: delegatedFrom
properties.definition: The right this was delegated from. Chains must end at a formal root right held by the root seat.

properties.name: authorityLimit
properties.definition: Monetary ceiling per decision. A constitutive rule of authority, not a measured value; same standing as lgl:contractValue.

properties.name: authorityCurrency
properties.definition: ISO 4217 code for authorityLimit.

properties.name: scopedTo
properties.definition: Scope entities (hr:OrgUnit, lgl:Jurisdiction, fin:CostCenter, log:Route); open range. Values of the same class are OR-ed and different classes are AND-ed. None = enterprise-wide.

properties.name: answersFor
properties.definition: The object the seat renders account for: Outcome, cmp:Risk, cmp:Control, fin:CostCenter, lgl:Contract, BoundaryObject. Open range, enforced by SHACL. Never a metric: seats answer for outcomes and are evaluated on metrics.

properties.name: accountabilityKind
properties.definition: outcome-owner | decision-accountable | cost-center | revenue-center | profit-center | investment-center | risk-owner | control-owner | definition-steward.

properties.name: bindsMetric
properties.definition: The metric the seat is evaluated on or reports. The measurement layer resolves which version is live in bindingPeriod. No values, targets or weights are held.

properties.name: bindingPurpose
properties.definition: evaluated-on (on the seat's scorecard) | reports-on (an information obligation up a channel; the attenuated signal made explicit).

properties.name: bindingPeriod
properties.definition: The evaluation or reporting period. Reuses Finance's calendar so scorecard and P&L periods line up.

properties.name: domainCode
properties.definition: Stable code; also the IRI local id (xfn:DecisionDomain/SUPPLIER-SELECTION-DM).

properties.name: domainOwner
properties.definition: The one function that owns the lever. A single owner is what makes cross-boundary exposure detectable.

properties.name: actsOnClass
properties.definition: IRI of the entity class the decisions select or set (fin:Vendor, fin:Budget, lgl:Contract). A literal because kg_edges cannot target classes. Single-valued: split a domain rather than list several classes.

properties.name: gapRight
properties.definition: Decider side: the in-force ratify or veto right.

properties.name: gapAnswerability
properties.definition: Bearer side: another seat's answerability for the outcome of the claimed effect.

properties.name: gapClaim
properties.definition: The claim the gap is conditional on. Withdraw the claim and the gap closes on re-derivation.

properties.name: convergesAt
properties.definition: The lowest common superior of decider and bearer over in-force solid lines: the first seat whose chain contains both ends. Absent = no common root.

properties.name: sharedForum
properties.definition: Collective seats that both decider and bearer sit on (via seatOn): lateral convergence points below the common superior.

properties.name: derivationRule
properties.definition: Versioned id of the published derivation, e.g. xfn:rule/exposure-gap@1.0.

properties.name: derivedAt
properties.definition: Derivation instant; also the as-of time for validity evaluation.

properties.name: gapStatus
properties.definition: open | closed. Set only by re-derivation. The gap closes when any premise lapses, including when the decider gains its own answerability for the outcome.

properties.name: decisionId
properties.definition: Stable id; also the IRI local id (xfn:Decision/PROC-2025-014).

properties.name: decisionStatement
properties.definition: What was decided, stated without reference to effects, e.g. 'replace primary supplier of component C'.

properties.name: decisionKind
properties.definition: Term in scheme decision-kind, e.g. supplier-switch, supplier-award, consolidation, specification-change, payment-terms-change, budget-cut, phasing-shift, hiring-freeze, sourcing-model-change, capital-allocation, accounting-treatment, cost-allocation-rule, concession, roadmap-deferral, deprecation, risk-acceptance, exception-action, regulatory-interpretation. Replaces per-function decision subclasses.

properties.name: inDecisionDomain
properties.definition: The lever this decision instance belongs to.

properties.name: exercisedRight
properties.definition: The right under which the decision was taken. Makes limit, scope and validity at the decision date checkable. A decision without it is reportable as unattributed authority.

properties.name: decidedBy
properties.definition: The accountable individual. Committees are recorded via decidedInCapacityOf a collective Position.

properties.name: decidedInCapacityOf
properties.definition: The seat in which the person decided. Answers 'who was CPO when this was ratified'.

properties.name: decidingFunction
properties.definition: The function on whose authority the decision was made.

properties.name: decidedOn
properties.definition: Date the decision was taken; the proposed date while status = proposed.

properties.name: effectiveFrom
properties.definition: Shared property, no rdfs:domain. On a Decision: the date it started landing on the business (e.g. first PO at new terms); lag zero for every claim about it, often months after decidedOn. On a MetricVersion: the first date whose observations bind to it, required once published.

properties.name: decisionStatus
properties.definition: proposed | approved | enacted | reversed | withdrawn. Proposed decisions let ex-ante claims attach to options a CEO has not yet taken. This is the status of the act, and it is excluded from the content digest.

properties.name: intervenesOn
properties.definition: The variables the decision sets directly: the do() target. Consequences are never listed here, including the one the decider is scored on; those are EffectClaims.

properties.name: baselineState
properties.definition: State of the target variables without the decision, i.e. the contrast baseline, e.g. 'V-2305 under ACME-CTR-0017'.

properties.name: interventionState
properties.definition: The state the decision sets, e.g. 'V-2688 under ACME-CTR-0101'.

properties.name: changesObject
properties.definition: Boundary objects the decision changes: the unit of analysis, on which other functions hold perspectives.

properties.name: involvesEntity
properties.definition: Module records the decision concerns: fin:Vendor, lgl:Contract, log:PurchaseOrder, fin:Budget, fin:CostCenter. Open cross-module range.

properties.name: consultedFunction
properties.definition: Functions consulted before deciding. Compared with the impactedFunction of claims about the decision, this is the Ashby variety check.

properties.name: consultationComplete
properties.definition: True = consultedFunction is exhaustive, so a function's absence means it was not consulted (closed world for this list only). Absent = unknown.

properties.name: statedRationale
properties.definition: The reasoning given at the time, in the decider's words, captured before hindsight.

properties.name: statedBenefitMetric
properties.definition: The metrics the decision was justified by. Recording what a decision was scored on is the precondition for asking what it was not scored on.

properties.name: declaredScope
properties.definition: local | cross-functional | enterprise: the scope the decider claimed at the time. The gap between a declared 'local' and a cross-functional landing is observable.

properties.name: reversalLeadTimeDays
properties.definition: The decider's stated estimate of days to undo the decision, including requalification. A stated planning parameter, not a measurement.

properties.name: supersedesDecision
properties.definition: A prior decision this one reverses or replaces.

properties.name: commitmentKind
properties.definition: Term in scheme commitment-kind: minimum-volume, exclusivity, rebate-tier, spend-commitment, service-entitlement, delivery-promise, roadmap-promise, price-concession, term-concession.

properties.name: commitmentStatement
properties.definition: The commitment in the words given to the counterparty.

properties.name: madeUnderDecision
properties.definition: The decision that created the commitment.

properties.name: commitmentCounterparty
properties.definition: The party the commitment is made to or received from. Union range stored null; enforced by SHACL.

properties.name: commitmentDirection
properties.definition: given (Acme owes it) | received (the counterparty owes it).

properties.name: isContractual
properties.definition: True only where evidenced in an executed lgl:Contract. How often it is false is the point of the field.

properties.name: capturedIn
properties.definition: contract | order-form | price-file | email | slide | verbal | tool-configuration | none. Where the commitment is actually visible to the functions that must honour it.

properties.name: evidencedIn
properties.definition: The contract or clause evidencing the commitment. Absent wherever isContractual is false.

properties.name: bindsFrom
properties.definition: Date it begins to bind.

properties.name: bindsUntil
properties.definition: Date it ceases to bind. Its absence is itself the exposure.

properties.name: exitTerms
properties.definition: Stated notice period, penalty or exit-cost basis: the switching cost that makes a decision practically irreversible. A term, not a measurement.

properties.name: judgedBy
properties.definition: The metric definition(s) used to judge performance against the commitment, e.g. an SLA's response metric, whose clock convention is in the version.

properties.name: deviationInContract
properties.definition: The contract in which the deviation occurs. Always present, including for absences, which is what makes an absence queryable.

properties.name: termKind
properties.definition: indemnity | liability-cap | warranty | termination-right | payment-terms | sla | data-processing | other. The typed discriminator that the lgl:Clause kind is supposed to be and, in the seed, is not.

properties.name: deviationDirection
properties.definition: more-favourable | equivalent | less-favourable | absent.

properties.name: deviatingClause
properties.definition: The clause that deviates. Null when direction is 'absent'.

properties.name: benchmarkContract
properties.definition: The contract compared against, e.g. the displaced supplier's contract. Together with the switch Decision, this makes 'we gave up the indemnity we used to have' a query.

properties.name: benchmarkClause
properties.definition: The clause in the benchmark contract that the deviation is measured against.

properties.name: standardReference
properties.definition: The internal playbook position or policy that the term fell short of, cited verbatim with its version.

properties.name: deviationApprovedBy
properties.definition: The person who approved the deviation. Its absence, where approval happened in a thread, is the highest-value query on this class.

properties.name: deviationApprovedOn
properties.definition: Approval date. A date later than the contract's effective date means the approval was retrospective.

properties.name: variableDefinition
properties.definition: What state or quantity this is, independent of any metric that measures it.

properties.name: valueType
properties.definition: binary | categorical | ordinal | count | rate | proportion | continuous. Needed to read sign: a categorical cause has no sign without a contrast.

properties.name: outcomeStatement
properties.definition: The outcome as a desirable state, with no numbers, e.g. 'few customer contacts caused by product defects'. A material change of meaning creates a new Outcome that revises this one.

properties.name: statedOver
properties.definition: The neutral variable whose state the outcome is about. This is how propagation maps a claimed sign on a Variable to good or bad for a function.

properties.name: preferredDirection
properties.definition: increase | decrease | maintain | within-band. Part of the outcome's meaning. Band limits and targets belong to the incentive layer.

properties.name: inRemitOf
properties.definition: The function(s) whose remit includes the outcome: exactly one for a functional outcome; several, or 'enterprise', for a shared one.

properties.name: hasConstituent
properties.definition: Definitional decomposition: by definition the outcome is made up of these. Example: total cost of supply = unit cost + expediting cost + cost of poor quality + uncovered liability. Acyclic, unweighted, never causal. Two or more constituents spanning two or more remits make an outcome shared.

properties.name: metricCode
properties.definition: Stable catalogue identifier (MET-nnn). Never reused or reassigned.

properties.name: metricName
properties.definition: The name as spoken in meetings, e.g. 'OTIF'. Deliberately not unique across definitions.

properties.name: definedByFunction
properties.definition: The function whose definition this is and which reports it. Two functions defining 'availability' produce two MetricDefinitions.

properties.name: reportedTo
properties.definition: The seat whose forum receives the metric: the channel through which it is raised to the C-suite.

properties.name: versionOf
properties.definition: The catalogue metric this version operationalises.

properties.name: versionLabel
properties.definition: MAJOR.MINOR. MAJOR increments exactly on a break in series.

properties.name: definitionText
properties.definition: Plain-language statement of what one value means.

properties.name: populationClass
properties.definition: CURIE of the KG class whose instances are the units of observation (fin:Vendor, log:Shipment).

properties.name: inclusionCriteria
properties.definition: Membership rule over the population, including every exclusion, e.g. 'excludes customer-caused delays, lines re-promised by agreement, intercompany'. Mandatory text, because exclusions move metrics further than performance does.

properties.name: populationPerspective
properties.definition: The function's perspective whose criterion defines the population, e.g. Finance's 'vendor'. Pins whose definition the metric uses, so two 'vendor' metrics over different populations read as two metrics, not as conflicting numbers.

properties.name: computationDescription
properties.definition: Formula in words or notation over ontology terms. Never executable code: implementations live in layer 3, keyed by this version's IRI.

properties.name: baselineDescription
properties.definition: What 'before' means for change-against-baseline metrics (savings, reductions), including the baseline method: last-paid price, budget, should-cost, supplier opening ask. Required for such metrics.

properties.name: recognitionEvent
properties.definition: Business event at which a contribution enters the metric: PO issue at new price, goods receipt, ticket creation, contract signature. Fixes the metric's time horizon.

properties.name: measurementBoundary
properties.definition: Where the clock starts and stops, and what pauses it, for duration and timeliness metrics. Examples: 'PO issue to supplier ship-ready; excludes transit and inspection'; 'against generation-N promise'.

properties.name: numerator
properties.definition: Component version above the line of a ratio.

properties.name: denominator
properties.definition: Component version below the line of a ratio.

properties.name: derivedFrom
properties.definition: Other component versions that a derived, non-ratio metric combines. Acyclic.

properties.name: unitIri
properties.definition: QUDT unit IRI in which every bound value must be expressed. For money, the ISO 4217 currency goes in currencyCode.

properties.name: currencyCode
properties.definition: ISO 4217 code for monetary metrics, and with it the FX basis.

properties.name: scaleType
properties.definition: nominal | ordinal | interval | ratio (Stevens). Constrains which arithmetic is meaningful: no sums or products of ordinal risk scores.

properties.name: accumulationType
properties.definition: stock | flow | auxiliary (XMILE). The binding contract for system-dynamics variables.

properties.name: valueDatatype
properties.definition: XSD datatype IRI of every bound value (xsd:decimal).

properties.name: hasDimensionBinding
properties.definition: The grain: one binding per dimension indexing an observation.

properties.name: supersedesVersion
properties.definition: The version this one replaces for new observations.

properties.name: comparability
properties.definition: comparable | comparable-after-restatement | break-in-series. Required whenever supersedesVersion is present. Makes mid-year redefinition visible instead of silent.

properties.name: lifecycleStatus
properties.definition: draft | published | deprecated | retired. Only published and deprecated versions may receive bound values.

properties.name: onDimension
properties.definition: The conformed dimension this binding indexes.

properties.name: rollupRule
properties.definition: sum | recompute-from-components | period-end | period-start | time-weighted-mean | minimum | maximum | not-derivable. The algebra permitted along this dimension; declared here, never executed here.

properties.name: dimensionOrder
properties.definition: 1-based position of this coordinate in the canonical observation key. Unique within a version.

properties.name: memberClass
properties.definition: CURIE of the KG class whose instances are coordinates (hr:OrgUnit, fin:Vendor, xfn:LegalEntity, fin:FiscalPeriod, log:InventoryItem).

properties.name: rollupPredicate
properties.definition: CURIE of the KG predicate from a member to its parent member (hr:parentUnit, xfn:parentEntity): the hierarchy propagation walks.

properties.name: timeUnit
properties.definition: OWL-Time unit IRI for calendar dimensions with no KG members (time:unitWeek).

properties.name: isTemporal
properties.definition: True for time dimensions.

properties.name: statement
properties.definition: The claim verbatim, in its author's words. Where the structured encoding disagrees, the statement is the record and the encoding is wrong.

properties.name: encodedBy
properties.definition: Who translated the statement into structured fields, when this was not the author. The claim stays draft until the author confirms the encoding.

properties.name: citesEvidence
properties.definition: Evidence the author relies on. Only the author cites evidence for their own claim. Others bring evidence through their own appraisals, so every evidence link is attributable.

properties.name: statedCredence
properties.definition: The author's own stated probability (0-1) that the claim holds. Quoted; never computed, adjusted, defaulted or aggregated.

properties.name: statedLikelihoodTerm
properties.definition: The verbal likelihood the author used, from the IPCC calibrated scale (virtually-certain ... exceptionally-unlikely). Stored as said.

properties.name: conditionalOnModel
properties.definition: Identifier of the external, versioned model (DAG, SCM, simulation) whose assumptions the claim depends on. Opaque to the ontology. Mandatory for claims authored by an AnalyticAgent.

properties.name: claimedCause
properties.definition: The variable whose change is claimed to produce the effect. When viaDecision is given, it must be one of that decision's intervenesOn variables.

properties.name: claimedEffect
properties.definition: The variable claimed to change as a result. Must differ from claimedCause.

properties.name: viaDecision
properties.definition: The actual or proposed decision the claim is about. It supplies the do() contrast and lag zero. All claims that share it are claimed effects of one decision; this shared node is 'the arrow no single system holds'.

properties.name: causeContrast
properties.definition: The baseline-to-alternative change in the cause, when no decision fixes it, e.g. 'per 60 additional days of payment terms'.

properties.name: claimedSign
properties.definition: Direction of change in the effect variable: increase | decrease | no-effect | non-monotonic | unknown-direction. Direction, not valence; valence comes from the Outcome stated over the variable. 'no-effect' makes exclusions first-class and owned.

properties.name: dependencyKind
properties.definition: The Pearl rung the claimant asserts: associational | interventional | counterfactual | definitional. Records what is claimed, not what the evidence supports.

properties.name: orientation
properties.definition: prospective (a forecast made before the cause changes) | retrospective (an explanation made after) | standing (a general dependency). A prospective claim must predate the decision's effectiveFrom.

properties.name: magnitudeBand
properties.definition: immaterial | minor | material | severe, relative to the effect variable's normal range, as the claimant states it. Deliberately coarse and ordinal so it cannot be summed.

properties.name: magnitudeStatement
properties.definition: The claimant's own words on magnitude, e.g. '+15-45% tickets', 'roughly triple'. A quotation for layer 2 to parse, never a value to aggregate.

properties.name: onsetLagMin
properties.definition: Shortest claimed delay from the cause change to effect onset, as a single-unit ISO 8601 duration (P3M).

properties.name: onsetLagMax
properties.definition: Longest claimed delay, in the same unit. The lag is exactly why no single function connects the two ends.

properties.name: temporalProfile
properties.definition: step | transient | accumulating | decaying | oscillating | unknown.

properties.name: claimedMechanism
properties.definition: The stated 'because', in prose. A claim with no mechanism cannot be falsified; SHACL warns.

properties.name: claimedMediator
properties.definition: Variables the claimant says the effect passes through. A hypothesis for layer 2, not structure the ontology uses.

properties.name: effectModifier
properties.definition: Variables the claimant says the size or sign of the effect depends on.

properties.name: allegedPathway
properties.definition: Standing handoffs through which the claimant says the effect travels. A structural hypothesis, not an asserted edge.

properties.name: allegedKind
properties.definition: What the claimant says crosses the boundary (carried-kind terms: work, cost, risk ...). Uses the same vocabulary as Transfer, so structure and allegation can be compared directly.

properties.name: scopeEntity
properties.definition: Entities delimiting where the claim is asserted to hold: product, route, vendor, region, fiscal period. Open cross-module range.

properties.name: originFunction
properties.definition: The function(s) the claimant says control the cause. This is the claimant's framing, recorded on the claim.

properties.name: impactedFunction
properties.definition: The function(s) the claimant says bear the effect; 'enterprise' = the whole business. This is the load-bearing edge of the topology that propagation walks. It sits on the claim so that decision-to-bearers is depth 2.

properties.name: proxyMetric
properties.definition: The metric claimed to indicate the outcome.

properties.name: forOutcome
properties.definition: The outcome the metric is claimed to indicate.

properties.name: operationalQuestion
properties.definition: The question the metric actually answers (GQM). Its gap from the outcome statement is where Goodhart lives.

properties.name: indicatedDirection
properties.definition: increase | decrease | within-band | non-monotonic: the movement of the metric that is claimed to signal progress on this outcome. It belongs to the claim, never to the metric.

properties.name: validityCondition
properties.definition: Ceteris-paribus conditions under which the metric is claimed to track the outcome, e.g. 'like-for-like specification, quality tier, delivery terms and risk allocation incl. indemnity'. Outside them the claim asserts nothing.

properties.name: coversOutcome
properties.definition: Constituents of forOutcome the metric is claimed to capture. Constituents that no proxy covers are the unmeasured tasks.

properties.name: assessedVersion
properties.definition: Versions against which the claim's evidence was gathered. A proxy not assessed against the live version is stale.

properties.name: divergenceOf
properties.definition: The proxy claim this divergence qualifies.

properties.name: divergenceMode
properties.definition: Terms in scheme divergence-mode: regressional, extremal, causal, adversarial (Manheim & Garrabrant); multitask-omission (Holmstrom & Milgrom); externality; horizon-mismatch (Forrester).

properties.name: triggerCondition
properties.definition: The behaviour or regime under which metric and outcome come apart, e.g. 'saving achieved by a lower quality tier or weaker terms', or 're-promising against generation-N dates'.

properties.name: outcomeAtRisk
properties.definition: Outcomes, often in other remits, that can deteriorate while the metric improves.

properties.name: observableVia
properties.definition: Counter-metrics whose movement would reveal the divergence (paired indicators). SHACL warns if none.

properties.name: mechanismClaim
properties.definition: The effect claims describing the mechanism. Referenced here, never asserted.

properties.name: forecastsMetric
properties.definition: The metric version projected. The value itself is held in layer 3, keyed by this claim's IRI.

properties.name: forecastPeriod
properties.definition: The period projected.

properties.name: forecastScope
properties.definition: Coordinates delimiting the forecast (fin:CostCenter, hr:OrgUnit, product), matching the version's grain. Open cross-module range.

properties.name: forecastMethod
properties.definition: run-rate | bottom-up | driver-based | top-down-target | management-override | pipeline-weighted. Top-down-target and management-override are forecasts in name only and must be distinguishable.

properties.name: consumedBy
properties.definition: Functions that have declared they plan against this submission (supply build, requisitions, facility sizing). The known blast radius of a revision.

properties.name: appraises
properties.definition: The record this appraisal takes a position on. It must already exist, which keeps appraisal chains acyclic.

properties.name: stance
properties.definition: endorses | disputes | qualifies | not-identifiable | abstains. The author's position, never the ontology's verdict.

properties.name: onAspect
properties.definition: Terms in scheme appraisal-aspect: existence, direction, sign, magnitude, lag, scope, contrast, mechanism, confounding, alternative-cause, evidence-validity, variable-definition, proxy-validity. Required when disputing or qualifying.

properties.name: advances
properties.definition: Records put forward with the stance: a rival EffectClaim, a refined estimate, an alternative Variable. Rivals are not assumed to be mutually exclusive.

properties.name: invokesVariable
properties.definition: Variables pointed to without claiming anything about them, e.g. an alleged confounder or a seasonal driver.

properties.name: evidenceClass
properties.definition: Term in scheme evidence-class: randomized-experiment, natural-experiment, observational-analysis, model-output, structured-elicitation, expert-judgement, case-anecdote, mechanistic-argument, documentary-record, external-study. Classifies the design; never ranks it.

properties.name: evidenceSummary
properties.definition: What the evidence shows and does not show, in the preparer's words.

properties.name: evidenceSourceSystem
properties.definition: The system the evidence came from. 'none: recollection' is valid and visible, so an anecdote and a regression never look alike.

properties.name: evidenceSource
properties.definition: KG artefacts the evidence rests on: cmp:Evidence, cmp:AuditFinding, lgl:Contract, lgl:Clause, fin:Transaction, log:Shipment, dtwin twins (prov:hadPrimarySource). Open cross-module range.

properties.name: sourceLocator
properties.definition: Locator of a source outside the graph: ticket export, dataset, report, layer-3 series, insight finding.

properties.name: observationStart
properties.definition: Start of the period covered. Whether the window starts before the decision took effect is a checkable fact.

properties.name: observationEnd
properties.definition: End of the period covered, so a consumer can check that it spans the claimed lag.

properties.name: selectionCriteria
properties.definition: Machine-readable predicate (SPARQL or DSL) that reproduces the evidence population, e.g. a ticket cohort, so the accused function can re-run it. Defines membership, never counts.

properties.name: comparisonBaseline
properties.definition: The evidence item this one should be read against, e.g. the two quarters before the switch. Declaring a baseline is semantic; computing the difference is not.

properties.name: readingOf
properties.definition: Identifier of the artefact interpreted, e.g. 'insight-rule:vendor-payment-without-contract' or 'nlq-intent:vendors-with-payments-no-contract'. The artefact's logic stays in its own engine.

properties.name: readingPerspective
properties.definition: The perspectives, on ideal-type boundary objects, whose criteria this reading uses for each term of the artefact.

properties.name: joinCriterion
properties.definition: How records from different modules are matched: same-node | same-source-key | same-entity (via BoundaryObject aboutEntity) | same-corporate-group (via parentEntity*). 'same-node' across modules is the R1 hazard, now visible.

properties.name: isImplemented
properties.definition: True for the reading the deployed implementation actually follows. At most one per artefact.

Also fin:Vendor, log:Route and hr:OrgUnit. This is the feature of interest whose state the variable describes.

Also lgl:Contract, fin:Budget, fin:CostCenter and log:PurchaseOrder: the records a decision concerns.
