extensionPoints.name: EP1 Effect-claim intake
EP2 Verdict write-back
extensionPoints.contract:
Set up:
- Register one xfn:AnalyticAgent per engine version, with agentVersion and accountableOwner.
- Record each run as an xfn:Deliberation (deliberationKind analysis-run) with concernsDecision.

Write verdicts:
- One xfn:Appraisal per appraised record, with appraises, stance, onAspect terms and citesEvidence.
- Set generatedIn to the run, attributedTo to the agent, onBehalfOf to the owning function, and conditionalOnModel to the model IRI.

The engine's own estimates and its assumed structure, including arrows it assumes absent, are EffectClaims attributed to the agent. Model assumptions are therefore visible and contestable like anyone else's.

Rules:
- The engine never mutates any existing record.
- xfn never aggregates appraisals, ranks appraisers or marks a claim settled.
- Effect sizes and posteriors stay in layer 2, keyed by claim IRI.

extensionPoints.name: EP3 Intervention anchors
extensionPoints.contract:
Every xfn:Decision has:
- decisionId, decisionStatement (no reference to effects), decisionKind;
- decidedBy (hr:Person), decidingFunction, decidedOn, decisionStatus;
- intervenesOn (one or more Variables), baselineState, interventionState.

What a causal layer can derive:
- Unit population: the instance BoundaryObjects in changesObject that exemplify the same ideal type.
- Candidate concurrent confounders: other Decisions on the same changesObject or intervenesOn variables, queryable by effectiveFrom.
- Counterfactual questions about CEO options: proposed decisions (status proposed). Their predicted effects exist only as prospective EffectClaims.
- Type-level lever family: inDecisionDomain -> xfn:DecisionDomain, which has a single actsOnClass and a single domainOwner.

extensionPoints.name: EP4 Observation binding
EP5 Series continuity
extensionPoints.contract:
Follow supersedesVersion and act on comparability:
- comparable: concatenate the series.
- comparable-after-restatement: recompute history under the new version first.
- break-in-series: never concatenate (SDMX OBS_STATUS B).

MAJOR increments if and only if there is a break in series. Each definition has at most one live version.

When a new version goes live, every ProxyClaim whose assessedVersion excludes it is stale. That list is the layer-2 retest queue.

extensionPoints.name: EP6 Proxy and divergence facts
extensionPoints.contract:
Two attributed claim types:
- xfn:ProxyClaim: proxyMetric, forOutcome, operationalQuestion, indicatedDirection, validityCondition, coversOutcome, assessedVersion, statedCredence.
- xfn:DivergenceClaim: divergenceOf, divergenceMode, triggerCondition, outcomeAtRisk, observableVia, mechanismClaim.

Derivable facts:
- Unmeasured tasks: Outcome constituents covered by no active ProxyClaim (the Holmstrom-Milgrom check).
- Self-attested proxies: ProxyClaim.onBehalfOf equals the proxy's definedByFunction.
- Paired indicators: the observableVia sets.

Layer 4 should attach targets, bands and weights to the key (ProxyClaim IRI or MetricDefinition IRI, Position IRI, fin:FiscalPeriod IRI). A target then inherits direction, validity domain and known failure modes.

The ontology holds no target, band, weight or payout.

extensionPoints.name: EP7 Accountability facts
extensionPoints.contract:
Agents are Positions (holder). Principals are answerableTo.

Available facts:
- Scorecard: MetricBinding evaluated-on, with bindsMetric and bindingPeriod.
- Authority: DecisionRight (overDomain, rightKind, authorityLimit, scopedTo, delegatedFrom).
- Consequence exposure: Answerability (answersFor, accountabilityKind).
- Internal-customer relations: Handoff handoffFrom/handoffTo/receiverCriterion.
- What a receiver has not agreed to bear: Transfer.acceptanceStatus.
- Claimant interest position: Claim.onBehalfOf.

Basis formal vs attested separates de jure from real authority. All assertions are valid-time bounded (validFrom/validTo) and immutable (changed only via revises).

The multitask gap is computable: an Answerability with no evaluated-on MetricBinding whose metric has an active ProxyClaim for the answered Outcome.

No incentive term is ever added to xfn.

extensionPoints.name: EP8 Forecast value binding
extensionPoints.contract:
The layer-3 store holds the projected value keyed by the ForecastClaim IRI, in the forecastsMetric version's unit and grain.

Guaranteed on the claim: submitter (attributedTo), recordedAt (the vintage, never back-dated), forecastPeriod, forecastScope coordinates, forecastMethod and consumedBy.

Revisions form a chain through revises. Forecast accuracy may be scored against the first, the last or any vintage by walking the chain. Which vintage counts is a layer-4 choice, made openly.

extensionPoints.name: EP9 Propagation topology
extensionPoints.contract:
Walkable relations:
(a) Outcome -hasConstituent-> Outcome: definitional, acyclic, unweighted, never causal.
(b) Outcome -inRemitOf-> BusinessFunction.
(c) Outcome -statedOver-> Variable, with preferredDirection. This maps a claimedSign to good or bad per function.
(d) Decision <-viaDecision- EffectClaim -claimedEffect-> Variable <-statedOver- Outcome, and EffectClaim -impactedFunction-> BusinessFunction. Decision-to-bearers is depth 2, within ADR-002's cap.
(e) Handoff handoffFrom/handoffTo, with its Transfers.
(f) Position solidLineTo/dottedLineTo/seatOn.
(g) MetricVersion hasDimensionBinding -> GrainDimension.rollupPredicate, with the rollupRule algebra.

Every relation a consumer may annotate either has its own IRI (claims, Handoff, Transfer, Perspective, DimensionBinding) or is a set-valued plain edge with a stable (s,p,o) key.

Division of labour:
- Layer 5 takes effect sizes from layer 2 and values from layer 3.
- An unappraised EffectClaim contributes nothing numeric.
- xfn defines no traversal weights or closure.

extensionPoints.name: EP10 Structural diagnostics
extensionPoints.contract:
xfn:ExposureGap nodes are produced only by the published rule xfn:rule/exposure-gap@<version>.
- IRI: xfn:ExposureGap/G-{first 16 hex of sha256(right|answerability|claim)}.
- Idempotent. When a premise lapses the gap is closed, never deleted.
- Fields: gapRight, gapAnswerability, gapClaim, convergesAt, sharedForum, derivedAt, gapStatus.

Companion named queries (stored nowhere):
- Variety deficit: the impactedFunction set of claims on decision d, minus d.consultedFunction. Valid only when consultationComplete = true.
- Missing return channel: an active claim whose impacted function has no Handoff back to the deciding function.
- Clause regression: a TermDeviation with direction absent whose benchmarkContract is the displaced arrangement's contract.
- Unstewarded boundary objects.

The ontology asserts nothing about a gap beyond its premises.

extensionPoints.name: EP11 Cross-module identity
extensionPoints.contract:
There is one sanctioned way to treat records from different modules as the same thing. Walk Perspective.representedBy to the shared BoundaryObject IRI, optionally continue via aboutEntity to xfn:LegalEntity, and use parentEntity* for group grain.

Guarantees:
- Each correspondence is attributed (attributedTo, identityBasis) and can be revoked by superseding the Perspective.
- owl:sameAs never appears in xfn exports.
- LegalEntity IRIs are opaque and permanent. Duplicates are deprecated with a replacement, never deleted or re-pointed.

Serve the four-hop join as a derived view; no shortcut edge is asserted.

Whose definition an artefact uses is declared by a Reading (readingPerspective + joinCriterion) or by MetricVersion.populationPerspective.

The only licence to merge two functions' definitions is an adopted PerspectiveCorrespondence with matchRelation exact and appliesInContext ctx.all (or the consumer's own context).

extensionPoints.name: EP12 Claim-type extension
extensionPoints.contract:
New claim kinds (constraint declarations, contribution-factor claims, opportunity-cost claims, churn attributions) are added as rdfs:subClassOf xfn:Claim or xfn:EffectClaim, in a consumer's own module or a minor xfn version.

They inherit the full provenance envelope (attributedTo, onBehalfOf, recordedAt, recordStatus, statement, citesEvidence, revises, contentDigest) and all SHACL on it.

Restrictions:
- They must not subclass PerspectiveCorrespondence, the only adoptable class. Empirical claims can never be 'adopted'.
- They must never be projected into a direct triple between their endpoints. The RDF 1.2 export form is rdf:reifies <<( s p o )>>.

extensionPoints.name: EP13 IRIs and standard export
extensionPoints.contract:
Namespaces and IRIs:
- Namespace: https://{client-base}/ontology/xfn/. Pin it before first external consumption.
- Classes: xfn:<Label>.
- Instances: xfn:<Class>/<stable-id>, minted once, never derived from mutable labels, never reused. Ids follow the EC-yyyy-nnnn / AP-yyyy-nnnn style, like AF-2025-014.
- Module key = prefix = xfn, so propsJson keys export in the right namespace today.

Versioning:
- Minor versions only add classes, properties and ControlledTerms.
- Removals go through owl:deprecated.
- Breaking changes bump the major version and keep old IRIs resolvable.

Data conventions: datatype properties are single-valued scalars; all multi-valued facts are object properties.

Artefacts:
- module Turtle/OWL/JSON-LD via exportModule;
- SHACL via shaclJsonToTurtle;
- ControlledTerm individuals with the instance export;
- a static xfn-alignment.ttl with PROV-O/SKOS/ORG subclass and subproperty axioms.

Meaning never depends on Ontos internals.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: One word covers four legitimate concepts: Finance's remit-to payee row, Procurement's managed trading relationship, Legal's signing entity, and Logistics' ship-from site. Picking one of them is exactly what makes R1 silently wrong in both directions.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- An ideal-type BoundaryObject 'supplier'.
- One Perspective per function, each with its own localCriterion and localClass (fin:Vendor, lgl:Party, log:Carrier).
- Pairwise PerspectiveCorrespondences, e.g. finance->procurement as close/semantic on facet 'identity grain', plus an adopted negated exact match.
- One instance BoundaryObject per supply arrangement. Its Perspectives point representedBy at each module's records, and aboutEntity -> xfn:LegalEntity (with parentEntity for group grain).
- R1 becomes several Readings: Finance joins on same-node, Legal on same-corporate-group. How their results differ is queryable.

reconciledConflicts.term: Savings / cost / unit cost vs total cost
reconciledConflicts.resolution: Procurement's negotiated delta against a baseline it chose and Finance's year-on-year reduction in recognised expense are both true in their own vocabularies. Unit price is a part of total cost of ownership, not a synonym for it.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- Two MetricDefinitions. Each MetricVersion carries a baselineDescription naming the baseline method, and a recognitionEvent.
- The Outcome 'lowest total cost of supply' hasConstituent unit-cost, expediting-cost, cost-of-poor-quality and uncovered-liability.
- A PerspectiveCorrespondence on the ideal-type 'cost': broad, hierarchyType partitive.
- Procurement's ProxyClaim coversOutcome only the unit-cost constituent.
- A DivergenceClaim with modes externality, horizon-mismatch and multitask-omission names the other three constituents as outcomeAtRisk.

reconciledConflicts.resolution:
There are at least four definitions, which routinely differ by 6 to 15 points:
- Operations: despatch vs the latest confirmed promise, at line or order grain.
- Logistics: carrier delivery within log:DeliveryWindow.
- Sales: against the generation-1 date.
- Procurement: supplier delivery vs the latest confirmation.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- Separate MetricDefinitions sharing metricName 'OTIF'.
- Each MetricVersion states its own grain (a DimensionBinding on order vs line), measurementBoundary (clock stop and promise generation) and inclusionCriteria.
- PerspectiveCorrespondences on the ideal-type 'on-time', divergenceKind semantic, with a compound AND for Sales.
- Promise generations stay in the source systems. The generation a version uses is stated in its definition.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: Procurement quotes PO issue to ship-ready. Logistics measures dock to dock. Planning needs reorder trigger to available-to-promise. Sales promises whatever figure reached it.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- measurementBoundary is required on every duration MetricVersion.
- A lead-time commitment is an xfn:Commitment whose judgedBy points at the version with the explicit boundary.
- Correspondences between the perspectives on the ideal-type 'lead time' are narrow/partitive: the supplier's segment is part of the replenishment cycle.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: Sales' margin is list price minus discount and contains no cost. Finance's margin tiers depend on allocation rules and which cost elements are in scope. Services means realised margin after delivery.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- One MetricDefinition per tier and per function.
- Allocation rules and cost-element scope are written into each version's computationDescription and inclusionCriteria, with derivedFrom pointing at the component versions.
- A DivergenceClaim records that excluding cost-to-serve lets Sales optimise its margin while Support's cost-to-serve outcome is at risk.
- No fin:MarginDefinition class is needed.

reconciledConflicts.resolution:
Five functions use the word differently:
- Finance: a non-cancellable encumbrance.
- Procurement: a PO has been issued.
- Revenue: the forecast category at 90% confidence.
- Legal: signed and enforceable.
- Operations: capacity is reserved.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- xfn:Commitment covers only promises to or from counterparties, with isContractual and capturedIn made explicit.
- Revenue's 'commit' is a ForecastClaim with method pipeline-weighted, never a Commitment.
- The PO-versus-encumbrance dispute is a pragmatic PerspectiveCorrespondence on the ideal-type 'committed spend'.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: In the existing seed, fin:Account is a GL account. Support's and Revenue's 'account' is a customer organisation, at a grain (tenant, logo, bill-to) that differs by function.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- xfn introduces no Account or Customer class.
- Customers are an ideal-type BoundaryObject 'customer'. Each function's Perspective records its grain in localCriterion and points representedBy at its own records.
- aboutEntity -> LegalEntity gives the payer and signatory referent.
- A negated exact correspondence protects fin:Account's meaning.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: For Legal, the contract is the executed document and its clauses. For Procurement, it is the whole commercial arrangement, including price files, rebates and side letters.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- lgl:Contract stays Legal's.
- The arrangement is an instance BoundaryObject. Procurement's Perspective includes the contract among its representedBy records.
- xfn:Commitments with isContractual=false carry the economics Legal cannot see.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: The eight experts proposed eight different status vocabularies. Several mixed discourse state with social agreement ('accepted-by-both-functions', 'corroborated'), or came close to asserting truth ('confirmed').
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- One speech-act lifecycle for every record: draft | asserted | withdrawn | superseded.
- Agreement and dispute are Appraisal records with a stance. 'Contested' is derived from the existence of a disputing Appraisal and never stored.
- There is no truth value anywhere, and SHACL patterns enforce this.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: cmp:Evidence means 'a control operated' and carries a 90-day freshness warning. Reusing it would put every cross-functional claim into the control-evidence staleness report.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- New class xfn:EvidenceItem, with evidenceClass (classified, never ranked) and a mandatory evidenceSourceSystem.
- cmp:Evidence and cmp:AuditFinding are cited through evidenceSource.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: Several experts used hr:OrgUnit as 'the function'. But the seed has no Procurement, Support or Legal unit, and org charts are re-cut every 12 to 18 months.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- xfn:BusinessFunction with a stable functionKey, performedBy hr:OrgUnit (many-to-many), and headedBy a Position.
- Claims, remits and handoffs all point at BusinessFunction.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: One word covers the definition steward, the accountable signatory, the team that runs something, the cost-centre owner and the party scored on it.
Support's S1-S4 measures customer impact. Engineering's SEV measures blast radius. cmp:severity measures audit risk. Finance's materiality is a threshold. The risk register's 1-5 scores are ordinal.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- Each scale stays in its source module.
- Any metric over them must declare scaleType.
- SHACL-SPARQL blocks deriving interval or ratio metrics from ordinal scores, which exposes R9-style arithmetic.
- Comparing severity across functions is a semantic PerspectiveCorrespondence, never a merged field.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: Support means a service disruption; Engineering, a SEV incident; Compliance, a notifiable breach on a 72-hour clock; Legal, a breach of contract.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- An ideal-type BoundaryObject 'incident' with one Perspective per function.
- The regulatory clock is the measurementBoundary of Legal's MetricVersion.
- A decision not to notify is recorded as an xfn:Decision (kind regulatory-interpretation) with decidedBy.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: HR counts filled employee seats. Finance counts budgeted FTE plus contingent labour. Operations counts productive hours. The same contractor is hr:Contractor to HR and fin:Vendor to Finance.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- Separate MetricDefinitions with explicit inclusionCriteria.
- Each contingent worker is an instance BoundaryObject with an HR Perspective (representedBy hr:Contractor) and a Finance Perspective (representedBy fin:Vendor).
- A sourcing-model-change Decision can therefore be traced to both sides, where R1 currently misattributes it.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: lgl:Regulation (legal instruments) and cmp:Regulation (control frameworks, including ISO 27001) are two classes with the same label and overlapping instances.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- Neither class is merged.
- Each record's Perspective points at a BoundaryObject whose aboutEntity is the legislation's ELI IRI. This makes the correspondence explicit, and shows that ISO 27001 is a standard, not a law.
- Whether to merge is left to the owners of those modules.

reconciledConflicts.resolution: The experts used Goal, StatedGoal, Outcome and proxyForGoal as a string. Several put polarity on the metric itself.
reconciledConflicts.modelledAs:
- One class: xfn:Outcome = a Variable + preferredDirection + remit + definitional constituents.
- Metrics relate to outcomes only through ProxyClaims, which carry indicatedDirection.
- Metrics themselves carry no polarity.

designRationale:
MERGES
(1) CLAIMS. Eight function-specific claim classes collapse into one xfn:EffectClaim under an AttributedRecord/Claim envelope: FinancialEffectClaim, CrossFunctionalClaim, ops:EffectClaim, ServiceImpactClaim, CommercialEffectClaim, CrossBoundaryAssertion/ExposureAssertion, SpilloverClaim, and the eng claim subclasses.
I chose the clm design because it is the only one that makes the endpoints neutral Variables and the do() contrast a shared Decision. That rules out three failure modes in the other designs:
- 'any node' endpoints, which the causal layer cannot bind;
- claims that point at a metric definition, which confuses the construct with its proxy;
- a direct saving->tickets edge, which is a confounded arrow between two effects of the same decision.
Magnitude is an ordinal band plus the claimant's quoted words, never a number, so layer 5 cannot sum claims and bypass layer 2.
The eight status vocabularies became one speech-act lifecycle plus Appraisal records. 'Contested', 'accepted-by-both' and 'corroborated' were pseudo-verdicts.

(2) DECISIONS. About twenty decision classes become one xfn:Decision whose kind is a ControlledTerm: FinanceDecision and its subclasses, SourcingDecision and its subclasses, OperationalDecision, WorkforceDecision and its subclasses, Concession, RoadmapDecision, ArchitectureDecision, DeprecationDecision, RiskAcceptance, LocalChange, Intervention.
The causal layer needs one intervention class. Subclassing per function would rebuild the silos inside the ontology. Kind-specific operational fields stay in the source systems, or become baselineState/interventionState text.

(3) METRICS. The met design wins: a mutable catalogue identity plus an immutable version that is the only binding target. It is the only design that supports series continuity, and series breaks are where redefinition gaming hides.
Population and ComputationSpec fold into MetricVersion properties. UnitOfMeasure becomes a QUDT IRI literal.
DimensionBinding and GrainDimension stay as classes, because shared grain is what makes 'no single system holds the arrow' queryable, and it is the rollup algebra layer 5 needs.

(4) GOALS. Goal, StatedGoal, Outcome and proxyForGoal strings become one Outcome: a Variable plus preferredDirection plus remit plus constituents. Claims stay free of valence, and propagation can still tell good from bad for each function.

(5) PROXY FAILURE. Gaming-risk, proxy-gap, substitution-risk and excluded-signal strings become ProxyClaim plus DivergenceClaim. They are attributed, contestable, and linked to counter-metrics and mechanism claims.

(6) IDENTITY AND TERMINOLOGY. Four identity mechanisms and three terminology mechanisms collapse into BoundaryObject + Perspective + PerspectiveCorrespondence, with LegalEntity as the real-world referent.
- Identity mechanisms merged: AccountAlignment, payeeVendor/sameAsCounterparty, clo:denotesEntity, aln:IdentityAssertion.
- Terminology mechanisms merged: aln Concept/Scheme/Correspondence, xfn Divergence, and the conflict lists.
Star & Griesemer's model does both jobs. Ideal-type boundary objects carry definitions; instance boundary objects carry records.
From aln I kept the rigour of graded matches: exact/close/broad/narrow, negation, compound targets, hierarchy type, contexts, and steward adoption.

(7) ACCOUNTABILITY. The acc design, as proposed: seats; DecisionRight, Answerability and MetricBinding kept separate (RACI's fusion of authority and exposure is exactly where externalities come from); and a derived ExposureGap.
Cut from acc:
- PositionAssignment: the Decision records decidedBy and decidedInCapacityOf instead;
- AccountabilityInstrument: cmp:Policy serves;
- the reified ReportingLine: replaced by solidLineTo and dottedLineTo.

(8) COMMITMENTS. Nine commitment and concession classes become xfn:Commitment. isContractual and capturedIn were the fields every expert called load-bearing.
Internal bearing becomes xfn:Transfer: obligationBorneBy, costBorneBy, ObligationAssignment and constrainsFunction all map to it. The same class serves standing Handoffs, so 'who bears it, and did they accept' has one representation.

(9) TermDeviation (from clo) is kept, because an absent indemnity can only be a node if the gap itself is reified, and it carries the approver. StandardPosition is cut; standardReference text and benchmarkContract replace it.

(10) EvidenceItem absorbs TicketCohort through selectionCriteria and comparisonBaseline. Reading absorbs aln TermBinding.

CUTS
Operational detail stays in the source systems and is reached through aboutEntity, evidenceSource or representedBy. Cut classes:
- Ticket, Incident, Defect, Change, Release, Service, FlowUnit, OrderLine, FulfilmentPromise, Nonconformance, CapacityPool;
- Category, SupplierSite, SourceQualification, SupplierScorecard;
- CloseCycle, ManualJournalEntry, CostAllocationRule, CostObject, Provision, Quota;
- Opportunity, Booking, Renewal, Customer, Contact;
- Capability, SeparationEvent, JobRequisition, HeadcountPlan;
- RegulatoryObligation, RemediationAction, ControlReliance, ObligationConflict, ThroughputConstraint.
Legitimate extensions among these belong to the owning module (hr, fin, log, lgl). New claim kinds plug in via EP12.
Nine code-list classes collapse into one ControlledTerm. Closed lists are string enumerations enforced by sh:pattern, the only enumeration mechanism the Ontos SHACL compiler emits.
Result: 35 classes.

IDENTITY
key = prefix = 'xfn'. rdfBridge qualifies unprefixed props with moduleKey, so every existing module whose key differs from its prefix exports undeclared namespaces; xfn does not.
Colour #A3E635 (lime-400): matches the 400-shade palette, and three experts converged on it.

CONVENTIONS USED IN THIS OUTPUT
- The string 'null' in domain or range stands for the Ontos null slot: either a shared property with no rdfs:domain, or an open cross-module range.
- Prefixed ranges (hr:Person, lgl:Contract) and union ranges ('A | B') are stored as null in PROP_DEFS, with the target named in the definition as a cross-module axiom (house precedent: hr:signs). SHACL sh:class, and sh:or/SPARQL for unions, enforce them, and those constraints do export. A one-line change to the seed loader, resolving any label that contains ':' across modules, would populate rangeClassId directly; ontologyRouter.createClass already does this.
- effectiveFrom is one shared property with no domain, used by both Decision and MetricVersion.
- Every 0..* fact is an object property, because knowledgeGraphToTurtle drops arrays.
- Values typed dateTime, duration or anyURI are also pattern-checked, until literal typing follows rangeDatatype.
- Overlay rule: xfn edges start at xfn nodes, and seed-xfn.ts wipes only xfn rows (precedent: seed-twins).

shaclNotes.constraints:
attributedTo: minCount 1, maxCount 1; sh:or of sh:class hr:Person | hr:OrgUnit | lgl:Party | fin:Vendor | xfn:AnalyticAgent (Violation).

recordedAt: minCount 1, maxCount 1; pattern ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T.

recordStatus: minCount 1; pattern ^(draft|asserted|withdrawn|superseded)$. Violation message: 'speech-act status only; truth is never recorded here'.

revises: maxCount 1; must point at a record of the same class (SPARQL).

contentDigest: pattern ^[0-9a-f]{64}$; required once recordStatus != draft (Warning).

SPARQL rules:
- withdrawn ⇔ withdrawnAt is present.
- attributedTo is an AnalyticAgent ⇒ onBehalfOf is present.
shaclNotes.rationale: No anonymous arrows: an unattributed claim is a rumour and must not be storable. The digest makes any breach of immutability detectable.

shaclNotes.constraints:
statement: minCount 1, maxCount 1 (Violation).

onBehalfOf: minCount 1, class xfn:BusinessFunction (Violation).

statedCredence: pattern ^(0(\.\d+)?|1(\.0+)?)$ (a value between 0 and 1).

statedLikelihoodTerm: must match the IPCC likelihood terms.

SPARQL: attributedTo is an AnalyticAgent ⇒ conditionalOnModel is present (Violation).

encodedBy differs from attributedTo ⇒ the claim stays draft until the author confirms it (Warning).
shaclNotes.rationale: Provenance is required on every claim, whether human or machine. A machine claim that depends on a model can never masquerade as a finding.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Endpoints:
- claimedCause and claimedEffect: minCount 1, maxCount 1 each; class xfn:Variable; SPARQL: the two must differ.

Classification fields:
- claimedSign: pattern ^(increase|decrease|no-effect|non-monotonic|unknown-direction)$.
- dependencyKind: pattern ^(associational|interventional|counterfactual|definitional)$.
- orientation: pattern ^(prospective|retrospective|standing)$.
- impactedFunction: minCount 1.

viaDecision: maxCount 1. SPARQL rules:
- claimedCause ∈ viaDecision/intervenesOn (Violation).
- orientation is prospective ⇒ recordedAt < viaDecision/effectiveFrom (Violation).
- dependencyKind is counterfactual ⇒ viaDecision or causeContrast is present (Warning).

Lags and magnitude:
- onsetLagMin and onsetLagMax: pattern ^P\d+[DWMY]$; SPARQL: same unit, and min ≤ max.
- magnitudeBand: pattern ^(immaterial|minor|material|severe)$.

Warnings: claimedMechanism minCount 1; citesEvidence minCount 1.

Global CI ASK, which must return false: any triple that links one xfn:Variable directly to another.
shaclNotes.rationale: The arrow must be an n-ary, attributed and falsifiable record between neutral variables. No direct causal edge may ever exist.

shaclNotes.constraints:
appraises: minCount 1, maxCount 1, class xfn:AttributedRecord.
- SPARQL: must not appraise itself, and recordedAt ≥ recordedAt of the appraised record (keeps appraisal chains acyclic).

stance: pattern ^(endorses|disputes|qualifies|not-identifiable|abstains)$.

stance is disputes or qualifies ⇒ onAspect minCount 1 (Violation).

onAspect: IRI pattern ControlledTerm/appraisal-aspect\.
shaclNotes.rationale: Every verdict, including the causal engine's, enters as an attributed position. A dispute must name its grounds.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Enumerations:
- matchRelation: ^(exact|close|broad|narrow|related)$.
- divergenceKind: ^(syntactic|semantic|pragmatic)$.
- adoptionStatus: ^(proposed|adopted|rejected|reconciled|plural)$.
- hierarchyType: ^(generic|partitive|instance)$.

SPARQL rules:
- All perspectives involved are on the same BoundaryObject.
- hierarchyType is present ⇔ matchRelation is broad or narrow.
- compoundOperator is present ⇔ there is more than one object.
- adoptionStatus != proposed ⇒ reviewedBy is present, and reviewedBy is the steward of the object.
- No pair may have both an adopted exact match and an adopted broad or related match.
shaclNotes.rationale: Terminology collisions are recorded as graded, attributed conventions that never name a winner. This is the only adoptable class.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Required: heldBy, perspectiveOn, localPurpose, localCriterion, validFrom (each 1..1, Violation).

representedBy: minCount 1 (Info).

BoundaryObject: fewer than 2 distinct heldBy functions across its perspectives (Warning).

Cross-module check: a lgl:withParty or log:poVendor edge between records that share no BoundaryObject (Warning: silent identity).
shaclNotes.rationale: Every cross-module join must state whose definition it uses. This is the fix for R1.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Required:
- decidedBy: 1..1, class hr:Person.
- decidingFunction: 1..1.
- decidedOn: 1..1, xsd:date.
- decisionStatus: pattern ^(proposed|approved|enacted|reversed|withdrawn)$.
- intervenesOn: minCount 1.
- baselineState and interventionState: 1..1 each.

SPARQL rules:
- Status is enacted or reversed ⇒ effectiveFrom is present (Warning).
- exercisedRight is present ⇒ that right's holder equals decidedInCapacityOf, and the right is valid on decidedOn (Violation).

exercisedRight: minCount 1 (Warning).
shaclNotes.rationale: Every intervention anchor is dated, owned and has an explicit contrast, so it can be bound to a causal model and checked against delegated authority.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Required text fields (1..1 each): versionOf, definitionText, populationClass, inclusionCriteria, computationDescription, recognitionEvent, unitIri, valueDatatype.

Enumerations:
- scaleType: nominal | ordinal | interval | ratio.
- accumulationType: stock | flow | auxiliary.
- lifecycleStatus: draft | published | deprecated | retired.

hasDimensionBinding: minCount 1.

SPARQL rules:
- supersedesVersion is present ⇒ comparability is present.
- Status is published ⇒ effectiveFrom is present.
- At most one live version per metric.
- rollupRule is recompute-from-components ⇒ components are declared.
- No sum or mean over ordinal or nominal values.
- No interval or ratio version derived from ordinal components.
- A published version depends only on published or deprecated components.
- dimensionOrder is unique within a version.
- The derivation graph is acyclic.
shaclNotes.rationale: Values can bind only to an immutable, fully specified definition. Redefinition and ordinal arithmetic become visible.

shaclNotes.constraints:
ProxyClaim:
- Required 1..1: proxyMetric, forOutcome, operationalQuestion, indicatedDirection, validityCondition.
- SPARQL: coversOutcome ⊆ forOutcome/hasConstituent*.
- Stale if assessedVersion does not include the live version (Warning).

DivergenceClaim:
- divergenceOf: 1..1.
- divergenceMode: minCount 1.
- triggerCondition: 1..1.
- observableVia: minCount 1 (Warning).
shaclNotes.rationale: Goodhart made structural: every proxy states what question it answers, when it holds, and what it leaves uncovered.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Outcome:
- statedOver: 1..1.
- preferredDirection: pattern ^(increase|decrease|maintain|within-band)$.
- inRemitOf: minCount 1.
- hasConstituent: acyclic (SPARQL).
- 2 or more constituents should span 2 or more remits (Warning).

Variable:
- aboutEntity must not point at any xfn:AttributedRecord (Violation).
shaclNotes.rationale: Decomposition stays definitional, and Variable-to-Variable edges cannot enter by the back door.

shaclNotes.constraints:
holder: 1..1, class Position.

basis: pattern ^(formal|attested)$.
- formal ⇒ grantedUnder is present.
- attested ⇒ evidenceRef is present.

DecisionRight:
- Every delegation chain reaches a formal root right.
- A delegated right may not exceed its delegator's limit or validity.

Answerability: answersFor is never a MetricDefinition.

MetricBinding: bindingPurpose pattern ^(evaluated-on|reports-on)$.

Position: solidLineTo forms a single-rooted tree (SPARQL).
shaclNotes.rationale: Accountability is recorded as sourced fact, with de jure and real authority kept apart. No incentive terms are admitted.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Transfer:
- transferOf: 1..1, must be a Handoff, Decision or Commitment (SPARQL).
- transferOf is not a Handoff ⇒ transferTo is present.
- acceptanceStatus is accepted ⇒ acceptedBy is present.
- transferBasis: pattern ^(designed|contractual|observedPractice)$.

Commitment:
- isContractual: 1..1.
- capturedIn: 1..1.
- SPARQL: isContractual is true ⇔ evidencedIn is present.

TermDeviation:
- deviationInContract: 1..1.
- SPARQL: deviationDirection is absent ⇔ deviatingClause is absent.
- deviationApprovedBy: minCount 1 (Warning).
shaclNotes.rationale: Unaccepted transfers and uncaptured commitments are the mechanism by which externalities arise. These shapes make them visible by default.

shaclNotes.constraints:
Required: gapRight, gapAnswerability, gapClaim, derivationRule, derivedAt (1..1 each).

gapStatus: pattern open | closed.

SPARQL: the IRI local id is G-{sha256(right|answerability|claim)[0:16]}.

Mutation guard: only the derivation job may create or close these nodes.
shaclNotes.rationale: Derived structure must be reproducible, and must never turn into a hand-asserted blame record.
